newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IT links seen adding US$500m to Canada-Asia trade.
newsitem.headline: IT links seen adding US$500m to Canada-Asia trade.

text.p: New Information Technology (IT) links could add as much as US$500 million to the value of trade between Asia and Canada over the next five years, a Canadian IT pioneer said on Tuesday.

"I expect US$500 million in trade between Canada and Asia in the next five years," because of the new links, said William G. Hutchison, group managing director of Canadian-based Quorum Growth International Limited.

He said the Pacific Network for the Advancement of Research, Industry and Education in Asia (PANARIE) would "build the technology bridge between Canada and Asia" and create an environment in which new trading opportunities would emerge.
PANARIE, still in its development phase but expected to be launched soon, aimed to have 200 Canadian and 200 Asian firms as part of its consortium within five years, he said.

Hutchison -- who founded the Canadian Network for the Advancement of Research, Industry and Education (CANARIE) in 1993 -- is leading the creation of PANARIE with the support of governments, businesses and universities from both regions.
CANARIE's billion-dollar program created the world's first longest multi media research and test network and funded more than 200 multi-media products and services.
The Telecommunications Authority of Singapore organised events encouraging joint ventures and PANARIE as part of the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair held in Singapore last week.

"The National Science and Technology and Enterprise Development Boards of Sinagpore have been very supportive of PANARIE," Hutchison said. "All sorts of Canadian companies want to be members," he added.
